'''Madhi-Madhi''', also known as '''Muthimuthi''' or '''Madi Madi''',<ref>*{{Cite book| last= ISO 639-3 Registration Authority| date = 2011| title = Change Request Number 2011-102: adopted create [dmd] (2012-02-03)| publisher = SIL International| location = Dallas| url = https://iso639-3.sil.org/request/2011-102}}</ref> is an [[Indigenous Australian language]] spoken by the [[Mathi Mathi people|Muthi Muthi]] Aboriginal people of south-west [[New South Wales]].<ref>Rees D. Barrett, Significant People in Australia's History, Issue 1 (Macmillan Education AU, 2009 ) p13.</ref> It is also known as Madhi Madhi, Madi Madi, Bakiin, Mataua, Matimati, Matthee matthee, Moorta Moorta, Mudhi Mudhi, Muthimuthi, Muti muti, Muttee Muttee, Madimadi, Mutte Mutte, or Madi madi.<ref name="AUSTLANG">{{cite web |title=D8: Mutti Mutti / Muthi Muthi |url=https://collection.aiatsis.gov.au/austlang/language/d8 |website=AUSTLANG |publisher=AIATSIS |access-date=16 May 2019 |language=en}}</ref>

[[Luise Hercus]] published in 1989 a substantial amount of Madhi Madhi language data recorded from Jack Long, whom she described as "the last Madimadi man" and the last speaker of the language.<ref name=":0">Hercus, L. A. [https://press-files.anu.edu.au/downloads/press/p72111/pdf/book.pdf#page=50 "Three linguistic studies from far south western NSW"], ''Aboriginal History'', 1989; v. 13 no. 1-2., p. 44-62. [https://web.archive.org/web/20210323211211/https://press-files.anu.edu.au/downloads/press/p72111/pdf/book.pdf Archived] 23 March 2021 at the [[Wayback Machine]].</ref>

/t̪, n̪/ are heard as palatal [c, ɲ] when before front vowels.

Voicing among stops /p, k, t̪~c, t, ʈ/ as [b, ɡ, d̪~ɟ, d, ɖ] may also be heard in syllable-initial positions or when following nasal sounds.

/t̪/ can be lenited as [θ] when in intervocalic positions, and as [ð] in post-nasal, word-medial position.
